candidate.title: Work
candidate.problemStatement: People responsible for one real outcome must reconstruct its state and next action from repository-local Initiatives, Assignments, workspaces, and settlement cuts even when those component records remain individually valid.
candidate.scope: Incubating higher-layer candidate for perspective-bound coordination across independently authoritative workspaces; independent object identity, cross-domain transfer, product qualification, numbering, and universal necessity are not claimed.

observationPerspective.bearer: human and agent participants designing multi-workspace agent coordination
observationPerspective.proximity: inside repository, workspace, graph, authority, and settlement implementation
consequences: bears routing, identity, graph, storage, migration, and qualification defects

genesis.observation: From the developer perspective, the natural response to cross-repository coordination was better workspace routing and a richer Assignment graph. From the person responsible for the outcome, those records were secondary to the state of the one body of work they jointly advance.
genesis.candidateObject: Work may be a higher-layer, perspective-bound coordinated action whole whose view preserves component authority, cuts, typed relations, proof state, degradation, and the current action frontier across workspaces.
genesis.claimBoundary: The cut opens qualification of Work and does not decide whether it is an independent object, a derived Work view, an Initiative or Portfolio projection, or no new Primitive.

transformedPerspective.bearer: a person using agents to advance one real outcome
transformedPerspective.proximity: inside progress, judgment, blockage, and continuation consequences but outside repository topology
consequences: bears context reconstruction, fragmented progress, missed judgment, and unclear next action

genesis.transformation: The observer moved from the developer managing component records to the person responsible for the outcome those components jointly advance.
genesis.newlyVisibleNeed: The user needs one inspectable action whole without treating repositories, workspaces, or card decomposition as the primary object and without losing exact component authority.
genesis.methodNotes: Initiative is retained as the strongest internal-object alternative; federation implementation and dogfood are future evidence rather than assumed facts.

contactSides: independently authoritative workspaces, Initiatives, Assignments, and settlement cuts
the person or agent responsible for understanding and continuing one real outcome
boundaryPressure.implicitHandling: The whole is reconstructed from parent-child cards, repository names, dashboards, chat context, branch state, human memory, and manual status summaries.

pressureChanges.description: One real outcome increasingly spans several repositories, workspaces, Assignments, agents, and settlements.
Component fact worlds remain autonomous and may use different Domain Profiles, availability, and lifecycle states.
Missing review, unavailable evidence, or incorrect aggregation changes what may safely continue.

observedFailures: A user must inspect repository-local cards to reconstruct one real work state.
Parent-child trees cannot express all dependency, contribution, continuation, conflict, and evidence-sharing relations.
A global summary may hide unavailable workspaces or pretend that several cuts form one atomic truth.
Child activity or stage readiness may be mistaken for accepted completion of the whole.
boundaryPressure.mediationClaim: A perspective-bound Work view may preserve one coherent action whole, component authority, and current frontier across independently owned fact worlds.
boundaryPressure.internalObjectAlternative: One Initiative, several related Initiatives, or a Portfolio query over a typed Assignment Graph may provide equivalent semantics without a new Primitive.

pressure: Real work spans several repository and workspace execution boundaries.
Users care about the outcome and next action more than execution location.
Autonomous fact worlds must remain independently authoritative and partially available.
Existing Initiative semantics may already absorb the proposed responsibility.
grounding.evidenceBoundary: The cut records situated maintainer judgment and public KFD contracts before a completed federated implementation. It contains no operational benchmark, independent adopter, non-software transfer, or proof that Work changes decisions beyond Initiative and derived-query semantics.
knownGaps: No independent Work identity or lifecycle witness
No decision between entity, derived-view, Initiative, and no-new-Primitive outcomes

alternatives.name: Initiative
alternatives.reason: KFD already accepts Initiative as one continuing coordinated software-work context spanning Pursuits, Assignments, participants, lineage, and settlement.

alternatives.name: Perspective-bound Work view
alternatives.reason: A root WorkRef, traversal policy, and component cuts may provide the user-level whole without a new semantic writer.

alternatives.name: Portfolio or saved query
alternatives.reason: A typed, cut-bound query may answer the same questions if it preserves observer, authority, degradation, and action-frontier semantics.

alternatives.name: Independent Work object
alternatives.reason: It remains possible that stable identity across several Initiatives and settlements changes continuation decisions, but no operational witness exists.

alternatives.name: No new Primitive
alternatives.reason: The current evidence is compatible with Work being only product vocabulary over existing objects.

contractModel.identity: Unresolved between a stable Work identity and a root WorkRef plus observer, relation policy, and component cuts.
contractModel.boundary: A declared coordinated whole, included workspace-qualified refs, typed edges, component cuts and proofs, unresolved or degraded components, action frontier, and declared loss.
contractModel.authority: Work may declare or project coordination but cannot replace owning workspace facts, transfer Warrant, prove occurrence, assess claims, decide admission, or synthesize a global Cut.
contractModel.lifecycle: Candidate lifecycle remains unspecified; possible views are derived at declared cuts, while an independent entity would require version, revision, split, merge, settlement, and supersession semantics.

minimumClosure.notes: The formal candidate closes a Work-view envelope but intentionally leaves independent entity identity and lifecycle unresolved.

deletion.notes: The analytic deletion argument identifies reconstruction burden but has not shown a bounded changed decision with fixed Initiative and Assignment roots.

fuse.notes: Possible separation from Initiative is stated but not demonstrated by an operational case where roots remain fixed and Work semantics vary independently.

falsifiers: Initiative plus Assignment Graph preserves equivalent identity, continuation, and settlement decisions at lower total cost.
Work membership is only a display query and has no stable decision consequence.
A Work-level object requires duplicate authority or a false global cut.
The view hides unavailable evidence, pending judgment, or independently variable lower responsibilities.
The model fails to transfer beyond one multi-repository software environment.

dogfood.notes: The workspace federation and Assignment Graph implementation is future evidence and is not represented as complete in this cut.

decision.owner: KFD maintainers subject to independent repository review
decision.reason: The observer shift and reconstruction pressure justify preserving Work as an explicit candidate, while existing Initiative semantics and the derived-view alternative prevent promotion or acceptance without implementation and comparative evidence.
residualRisks: The candidate may duplicate Initiative or Portfolio semantics.
The attractive user-level name may be mistaken for ontological evidence.
A central implementation could violate workspace authority boundaries.
A derived view may vary too much by observer and policy to carry stable identity.
The current evidence is first-party, software-oriented, and pre-implementation.
